sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Cleveland County?
sections.html:
Cleveland County Tax Administration, in the county administration building at 311 East Marion Street in Shelby, appraises property and bills and collects the tax. The office phone is 704-484-4843, and its website lists weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

The tax administrator's site describes a county of 469 square miles that includes 15 municipalities and says the office mails and collects more than 60,000 tax notices each fall. It offers a record lookup, an online payment search, an address change request and a tax estimator.

sections.h2: How often does Cleveland County revalue real property?
sections.html:
State law requires a reappraisal at least every eight years, but Cleveland County says it is on a four-year cycle. Its most recent revaluation took effect January 1, 2025.

The county's revaluation page explains that values are set as of that date from aerial and street photography, recent sales, land records and details such as zoning, soil class and improvements. Owners received notices in mid-February 2025. An earlier revaluation took effect in 2021, and a county news release says the commissioners cut the rate from 57.0 cents per $100 to 54.75 cents afterward.

For a seller, the practical point is that the tax value on a Cleveland County parcel reflects a January 1, 2025 snapshot, not today's market.

sections.h2: What is the Cleveland County property tax rate?
sections.html:
The County Manager's recommended 2026-2027 budget keeps the county rate at 40.5 cents per $100 of valuation. Added to a public school rate and a fire tax rate, the news release puts the total at 61.5 cents per $100.

Confirm the adopted figures and any city or town rate with the tax office, because the release describes a recommended budget and a June public hearing. Ask the tax office which school, fire and municipal rates apply to your parcel.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Cleveland County property value?
sections.html:
You can file a written appeal online, by mail or by email, or request an in-person meeting. The county says appeals are not taken over the phone.

  • Online: use the appeal form on the county tax site, one form per parcel.
  • Mail: send a photocopy of the form to the Cleveland County Tax Assessor, P.O. Box 370, Shelby, NC 28151.
  • Email: tax.assessor@clevelandcountync.gov.
  • In person: complete the request form attached to your notice and call 704-484-4911 for an appointment.

Plan on at least eight weeks for a mailed decision, and note that a review can leave the value unchanged, lower it or raise it. The county accepts two reasons: the assessed value is well above market value, or the property was appraised unfairly compared with similar properties. It does not consider the size of the increase, an insurance value, a feeling that value is simply too high, or inability to pay.

If the informal result does not satisfy you, state law lets you ask the Board of Equalization and Review for a hearing before it adjourns, in writing. That board is the county commissioners unless a special board is created. A further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mails its decision.

sections.h2: Does a higher appraisal always mean a higher Cleveland County tax bill?
sections.html:
No. The county's explanation is that a bill equals the tax value multiplied by the rate, and each taxing jurisdiction sets its own rate. After a revaluation some bills rise, some fall and some stay about the same.

The tax office says it can only act on the appraised value. Concerns about service levels or affordability belong with the elected boards that set rates, not with the appraisers. Before you appeal, open the county's assessment records map and turn on the Improved Sales and Vacant Sales layers, which the county recommends for finding recent comparable sales near your parcel. Personal property such as vehicles, trailers and boats is valued every year, while land and buildings are valued only at a countywide revaluation.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs does Cleveland County offer?
sections.html:
Three state programs are available through the county tax assessor. Most applications are due June 1, and each owner can use only one of the three.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: excludes the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of the appraised value of a permanent residence. The owner must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, and income must not exceed the limit, which is $38,800 for the 2026 tax year.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: excludes the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: caps tax at 4 percent of income up to the limit and 5 percent above it up to 150 percent of the limit, which is $58,200 for 2026. The owner must have lived in and owned the home for five years. A new application is filed every year.

Deferred circuit breaker taxes for the prior three years come due if the home is transferred, so a sale ends the deferral and puts those taxes on the closing statement. The county also describes a present-use deferral for farm and forest land, which taxes at use value but keeps the deferred amount on the books.

sections.h2: When are Cleveland County taxes due, and what happens if they are not paid?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1 and become delinquent after January 5. The 2025 relief notice said bills would be calculated and mailed in July after boards set rates.

From January 6 the delinquent balance carries 2 percent interest, and from February 1 it accrues three-fourths of 1 percent each month. A lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, so a seller cannot walk away from an unpaid year at closing.

When a county forecloses for unpaid tax, the county's tax foreclosure page shows the process. Auctions happen in the Commissioners' Room on the second floor of the administration building, and the winning bidder pays a 5 percent deposit. Each upset bid must beat the last by $750 or 5 percent, whichever is greater, and must be filed in person with the clerk of superior court. A new ten-day period starts after each one. The owner can redeem before the court confirms the sale.

sections.h2: What do I do about tax due when I sell a Cleveland County house?
sections.html:
Ask the tax collector for a statement of the current balance, and have the closing attorney pay it from your proceeds. That keeps the lien from following the buyer.

Delinquent years are paid in full at closing, with interest. If a parcel is already in foreclosure, the county's page says liens against it can be found in the complaint in the clerk's file, and you need the CV file number to pull it at the courthouse at 100 Justice Place in Shelby.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Cleveland County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts shows 103,325 residents in July 2025 and 45,667 housing units. The owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024 is 70.9 percent, the median owner-occupied value is $200,000, and median owner costs with a mortgage are $1,257 a month.

Median gross rent is $914, and 555 building permits were issued in 2025. Persons in poverty make up 16.3 percent of the population.

faqs.q: When are Cleveland County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1 each year and are delinquent after January 5. Interest starts January 6 at 2 percent, then three-fourths of 1 percent per month from February 1.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Cleveland County property value?
faqs.a: File a written appeal online, by mail to P.O. Box 370, Shelby, or by email, or ask for an in-person appointment at 704-484-4911. The county does not take appeals by phone, and a mailed decision can take at least eight weeks.

faqs.q: Does Cleveland County revalue every eight years?
faqs.a: No. State law sets the eight-year maximum, but the county says it is on a four-year cycle. The latest revaluation was effective January 1, 2025.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for tax relief in Cleveland County?
faqs.a: Most relief applications are due to the tax assessor by June 1 of the tax year. The elderly or disabled exclusion, disabled veteran exclusion and circuit breaker are all filed with the county, not the Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Cleveland County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the tax collector for the balance and have it paid from the sale proceeds at closing. If the county has already started a foreclosure, the owner can redeem before the court confirms the sale.
